And it's extremely difficult for the Prosecution to label documents as tending to be exculpatory, and the same would be true if the Chamber would have to rule on documents, because what we want to avoid, and I take it from the discussion yesterday in 65 ter, is that ever the Trial Chamber has more evidence available and to decide on evidence which is not available for the Defence, we have to obey the Rules, that this is a party-driven procedure, and it should be for the parties, for us, to try to come to an agreement. But unfortunately, from my point of view, if I may give this comment, the Judges should never have more access to documents than the parties have. So the remaining point, apparently, is that the Defence of Mr. Jokic feels that there are -- there would be a statement missing, and they request the entire -- an entire statement. I think this can be resolved on a bilateral basis. And only based on unfortunate experience in another case, and I have no doubt this -- that this will happen in this case as well, when a statement is disclosed, the entire statement has to be disclosed, and there is no discretion for the Prosecution to present only parts of the statements which they believe are of exculpatory nature. So I expect and I have no doubt that this will happen, that the entire statements are disclosed, and I would ask in this case both Defence counsel of Mr. Jokic and the Prosecution to try to come to a solution under Rule 68 and to point out what are the concrete statements they Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. believe that are missing. And only then later, if you can't come to an agreement, the Trial Chamber will rule on this. When preparing now for the trial, we should all try to do the very best to prepare whatever possible in order that it not need to be heard or introduced in live testimony, for example, during trial. The use of depositions, pursuant to Rule 71, is no doubt an ambiguous question, and sometimes from this there are emanating new questions, and the risk is extremely high that the one or other side wants a person to come back because the one or other question was not put to this question [sic]. But no doubt that the Defence would have the right to be present during taking such a deposition. Is it the intention of the Prosecution to prepare those depositions pursuant to Rule 71 in the eve of May 2003?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are still trying to sort that issue out, because there's several logistic problems related to the size of this case in trying -- if it was done in Bosnia or outside the Netherlands, as you say, each defendant would have a right to have counsel present, and as you know, counsel lives all over the world. And if it occurred in the Netherlands, these courtrooms are pretty filled up. So we're still exploring the logistics of being able to do this. I would like to try to look into anything that would save time, and so we continue to do that. But we have not made a final decision on that point yet, and I would like to talk to my colleagues in the Defence. I believe Mr. Karnavas has indicated that he would like his clients to be present, or his client to be present, during any such deposition, and so we may need to go to litigation on the matter, and that may defeat the very purpose that was designed to try to alleviate. So first I think I need to talk fully more to Defence counsel, and also to yourself and Mr. von Hebel, to get an indication of where the Court may be leaning on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this question is not ripe for a final discussion. Any additional remarks by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just one very quick one. I do believe that the client should be present at a deposition, especially the nature of why we're holding the deposition. I don't have any objections to having depositions, especially if they're here. It's convenient. They should be videotaped, of course. I don't know how that helps in shortening the time, because the Trial Bench is still going to have to watch, not just read, because you need also look at the demeanour of the witnesses. I think that's very important in assessing their credibility. I'm not opposed to it, but, as I indicated to Mr. McCloskey and I indicated to the other folks yesterday, that I will insist: I do think he has a right to be present. And of course, his presence is also necessary to assist his Defence counsel in any follow-up questions that they may have missed. So at least I'm on record as to why -- what our position is with respect to depositions. And I'm not trying to be an obstructionist, but I think it's necessary for the client to be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To be honest, I'm really hesitant whether or not depositions pursuant to Rule 71 really can save time. As mentioned, we would have to review not only the transcripts, but also see the video. And in addition, counsel, at least counsel - I don't want to rule on the question of the presence of a client - but counsel has a right to be present, and it's not only time-consuming but extremely expensive. But what indeed can assist in speeding up the trial, without infringing the right to due process or fair trial, would be the attempt - and I have to invite the parties to proceed with this attempt with all priority - to come to agreed facts. We have, during trial and after trial, to decide on the individual criminal responsibility of the four accused sitting in this courtroom today, the individual criminal responsibility. And from experience of other cases, we all know that the most problematic issue is to present, during the Prosecution's case, the evidence related to the chapeau elements of crime. This is, for example, the existence of an armed conflict, of a widespread, systematic attack, and so on. The Defence should assess whether or not they believe that there might be a possibility, maybe based on new evidence, to come to other conclusions than those conclusions you can find in a number of decisions issued by this Trial Chamber. This does not mean, of course, that any of the Judges hearing the case have made up their minds on this concrete issue related to this concrete area. But it would be extremely helpful, and I think it would also be extremely helpful for the accused themselves, if we could concentrate the trial on the question of the individual criminal liability of these individuals, of the concrete human beings accused in this case, and therefore, please - and this goes to both parties - try your very best to come to agreed facts, especially on these chapeau elements of crime. Are there any impediments identified already now by any Defence counsel related to this question of coming to agreed facts? May I ask you in the order once again. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if the question -- if you're asking me: "Is there goodwill for us to sit down and try to reach some agreed facts?" the answer to that question is yes. To the extent how many facts we can agree on, I don't know, but I certainly am willing, and I've also suggested that we do sit together and try to agree to the facts and to -- I'm sure that there are lots of witnesses, based on the Krstic trial, that may not necessarily need to be here. I'm sure the Prosecution may want some of those witnesses here. We may not feel that they're necessary. That's their call, of course. But I don't think that it's impossible to sit down and to agree to certain facts. But I can't guarantee that -- you know, the volume of the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Wilson, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the accused Obrenovic, through his counsel, has announced in this case, from the moment that we entered into it, that we were amenable to such agreements and that we have no intention of contesting each and every line of the indictment. For us, it is a matter of timing. It is not a matter of me, the lawyer, agreeing that this is the easiest and best way to go. I also have to explain to Mr. Obrenovic and he has to be comfortable with what I'm doing. All of this revolves around getting to him, as early as possible, these key documents that Your Honour has referred to earlier as needing to be translated. We remain very much agreeable to that. We have no interest in being in this courtroom any longer than necessary to get this resolved, and that has been our position from the beginning and it remains our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of the accused Dragan Jokic also absolutely supports this initiative, this need and obligation to coordinate with the Prosecution and agree on the facts which can be agreed upon. I believe that the Trial Chamber is absolutely clear that at this point in time, when we do not have the Butler report, it is very hard for us to say to which extent we can agree on facts. But I believe that there are agreed facts. There shouldn't be a problem. And our communication and cooperation with the OTP will certainly lead to the agreement on non-disputable facts. I also support Mr. Wilson's proposal that it would be important for the coordination to be done together with the OTP and that all the Defence teams attend such meetings and be present at such coordination leading to agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And on behalf of Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Londrovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence for the accused Nikolic also does not object to this manner of work. Yesterday we already started talking about certain facts at the meeting with the OTP. We raised some issue. But it will certainly take us much more time to agree on facts. And the Defence will certainly not avoid agreeing on some facts. And I also support my colleagues who say that it would be the most rational way to do it together, and only if there are specific facts which apply to only one accused, then we should work with the OTP individually. Already yesterday we started discussing some things with the OTP, and as far as our Defence team is concerned, there will be no obstacles to the extent which will not prejudice our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this willingness expressed by all parties for cooperation. Nevertheless, based on good experience in another case, I want to emphasise that, on the request of one or more parties, the Pre-Trial Judge in this case, or the Trial Chamber, is prepared to discuss these issues in order to come to such agreed facts and to discuss certain issues where the one or other party believes this shouldn't be discussed in open court. The Rules explicitly provide, under 65 ter (I), to have a meeting in the office of the Presiding Judge, and this should be seen as an opportunity to overcome problems, remaining problems, that we can start really concentrating on the core issues of the case before us. Please don't hesitate to take this opportunity. I'm always prepared to confer such a 65 ter (I) meeting. As mentioned before, it is already provisionally scheduled, and we have already asked the President to request the Secretary-General United Nations to appoint ad litem Judges for this case starting 6th of May. There has to be a Pre-Trial Conference beforehand. The next Status Conference would be due 26th of March. To avoid duplication, the intention is to have the Pre-Trial Conference during this last week of March. Maybe it can be helpful that already today the parties come together with Mr. von Hebel and discuss possible dates, envisaging already now that the Pre-Trial Conference may take us two days. I know that -- I think it was Mr. Obrenovic wanted to take the floor, but may I first of all ask counsel: Are there any other issues to be discussed during this Status Conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would just like to alert you to one issue as I -- that we probably can't decide now, but something that I think is good for the Status Conference. As I mentioned earlier, we do have some statements from witnesses that would be material to the preparation of the Defence. However, those statements were taken confidentially, and we don't intend to use the information at trial or use those witnesses in any way. And the disclosure of those witnesses could lead to the injury or death of those persons. And I believe Rule 66(C) is one of the Rules that goes to this particular issue, and it says that: "Where information is in the possession of the Prosecutor, the disclosure of which may prejudice further or ongoing investigations, or for any other reasons may be contrary to the public interest or affect the security interests of any State, the Prosecutor may apply to the Trial Chamber sitting in camera to be relieved from an obligation under the Rules to disclose that information. When making such application, the Prosecutor shall provide the Trial Chamber (but only the Trial Chamber) with the information that is sought to be kept confidential." Now, I have been telling trial -- Defence counsel that we were gathering our -- some of our people that fit this particular security concern and that I would be seeking the protection of 66(C). And the reason I raise that as a potential problem, in that some of this material could be inculpatory to the clients, to their clients, and the Defence counsel obviously would not be having a chance to see this material, for the security concerns. And as you yourself have said, that there's a potential problem when the Judge and the Prosecutor know about something that the Defence counsel don't know about. So we have various interests here, and predominantly I'm concerned about the interests of the few people that speak to us confidentially, as in any investigation, and that they not be risked. But I also, of course, have all these other concerns, and it just bears some thought on all parties to see how best to manage this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe your submission is an extremely good example for the way of working of the Prosecution: Instead of leaving this disguised, making reference in open court to these documents, to vulnerable witnesses, and this difficulty to apply Rule 66(C). Are there any comments related to this issue? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I appreciate the Prosecution's concern and I understand fully what his -- the dilemma that he's in. I do have some concerns, however, that we will not even have an opportunity to at least know the general gist of what it is that he's trying to protect. I don't have a problem with him protecting the sources or protecting the names, but I do think that if he's asking, which he is, for an in-camera review, I think that at some point we may benefit if we could have, maybe at the next -- at the Pre-Trial Conference, if we could have a closed session, where at least the Prosecutor could, in general, without giving any detail, in general tell us what it is. Because at least, one, we have a record from which -- at least I can then make a counter-proposal. But I certainly would like to know, in general, what it is that these witnesses may be saying, you know, the nature -- I don't want their names, I don't want -- I don't need any other sensitive information, but I think that would be -- I think it's appropriate, and I don't think that the Prosecutor would object to that minor request that I'm making.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please take it as guaranteed that both -- I think -- I can hear it from the approach taken by the Prosecution and the Judges, we will do whatever possible to overcome the difficulties emanating from this Rule 66(C). We have to apply this Rule, but there might be a solution, and we will do the very best to inform the parties, yes, on what can be disclosed. We have to discuss this, but then in concreto and not in abstracto. Any other issues to be raised by the parties?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, just on that same issue: As far as the Prosecutor divulging this information, I think it might be in the best interests of all of us to work together if he told us, you know, what these -- let us see these, because we've signed confidentiality agreements, and we're officers of the Court, that we should see these statements, and then once we determine whether we want to use them or whether they are material to the Defence, then we would proceed under 66(C).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. We are aware of this problem, and I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. only have to emphasise that deliberately it reads: " ... but only the Trial Chamber." I'm not the author of this Rule, but we have to obey this Rule. Any additional issues to be raised? I can't see any. So may I ask finally, in conclusion of this Status Conference: There was a point to be raised. I think it was Mr. Obrenovic. You wanted to take the floor? Or was there one --

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I think it was Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. Then Mr. Blagojevic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the issue of my defence in this case. The issue at hand is the following: The Defence counsel has been appointed in my case, and I have not agreed to that. And in those terms, I believe that certain problems have arisen that may impair the work and may lead to certain further consequences which I may not envisage. I have taken some steps, but they have been rejected, and I believe that the only solution that remains for me is to address the Chamber and ask you to consider the situation and make a certain decision. This is what I wanted to say in my introduction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this is not an issue that should be discussed in open court, and we will find a possibility to discuss it with you and the Defence counsel later. Please be assured we will not forget this issue. Please be seated. Thank you. I can't see any other requests for the floor. This concludes today's Status Conference. And please contact Mr. von Hebel as to the dates foreseen for the Pre-Trial Conference. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
